# 0.15.154

**The phone: calls the way a phone does them, a profile that looks like one, and the controls that
did nothing.**

Derek's second pass on a real phone — "this is about a 50% improvement… there is so much wrong with
it that the rest of the way will probably be very slow" — with the list he gave, and what walking
the app as a person found beside it.

## Calls, gone over end to end

- **A call is not a banner over a conversation any more.** "I dont want call banners on this app —
  Discord does not have little call banners hanging over chats ever." The strip above the stream is
  gone. A call you are in is the floating tile, everywhere but the call's own screen.
- **The tile shows one thing:** the picture of whoever is speaking, or spoke last. No camera, no
  mute pip, no caption. What it is doing is the ring around it — green while they talk, a pulse
  while it is still ringing.
- **The green ring survives a camera.** It was an inset shadow, which paints under the `<video>`
  that fills the tile, so turning video on took the ring away. It is drawn over the tile now.
- **The sound has a chooser.** The speaker control in the call opens the outputs this phone's own
  audio service reports — earpiece, speaker, a headset, a Bluetooth device — and moves the call to
  the one you pick. In a window it is the machine's outputs through `setSinkId`. A device that
  offers no choice says so rather than showing a menu that does nothing.
- **A phone could not hear a call at all.** A WebRTC track makes no sound on its own, and the phone
  had no `<audio>` anywhere: a call with the camera off was silent, and its deafen button changed
  nothing. Every remote voice now has its own element, with the volume, the muting rule and the
  chosen output on it — one module the window uses too.
- **Six controls fit the narrowest phone.** The dock's buttons share the row instead of each
  claiming 52 px.

## A profile that reads as a profile

- Opening somebody opens a card: their banner, their picture over it, their name, what they say —
  not a list of rows that reads like settings. Your own profile is the same card.
- **Banners, with somewhere to set them.** The Account page opens with your banner and lets you
  change it and your picture; a space's banner is across the top of its channel list.
- **One tap opens a conversation.** A person's name in Friends or in search opens the conversation;
  their picture, and a long press, open the profile. It used to take two taps to reach a DM.

## Things that did nothing, and now do

- **Mark unread.** The core's read marker only ever moved forward, so marking a message unread was
  a control that changed nothing at all. There is a command for it now (`mark_unread`), and doing it
  takes you back to the list where the count is.
- **Sending a picture.** Every picker row in the Send sheet is the file input itself, and so are the
  picture and banner rows on the Account page. A hidden input clicked by script one `await` after
  the tap is refused by a phone — which is what "I can't send images on mobile" was.
- **Holding a reply.** A message you answered could not be held by the quote of what it answered, so
  edit, pin, forward and delete were out of reach on exactly the part you were looking at.
- **A held message stopped looking held** once its menu closed.

## Everything arrives

"Nothing should just instantly appear. Everything is an animation." A message arriving while you
read rises into place the way one you send does; a staged picture, somebody else's reaction, a card
a link grew, a row a list gained and a line that says something changed all arrive with a movement.
What was already there when a screen opened arrives with the screen.

## Appearance, widened

Follow the phone's own dark or light, seven themes, accent hue *and* strength, four backdrop depths,
text size, line spacing, three corner roundings, picture shape, message layout, reduce motion — with
a live sample of the stream at the top of the page. Every control is a real input to the theme;
one that cannot change anything in the mode you are in says so.

## Also

- An empty conversation puts its introduction in the middle of the screen instead of pinning it
  above the composer under a screenful of black; a screen with nothing but an empty state centres it.
- A link's card had tighter padding than anything else and nothing telling a long word to break.
- The message field had a scrollbar down the middle of it.
- A muted conversation looks muted, rather than carrying one small grey bell.
- Editing a message keeps the card under it: an edit that names no card is an edit of the words.
- The phone's interface, every surface, on one page for a desktop screen:
  `node scripts/phone-sheet.mjs` → `test/out/phone-ui.html`.
